title: How to plan for a commercial lease expiry
excerpt: A practical sequence for checking dates, obligations, workplace needs and alternatives before a lease decision becomes urgent.
metaTitle: Commercial Lease Expiry Planning | Your Office Space
metaDescription: Plan a commercial lease renewal or relocation by checking key dates, obligations, workplace needs and alternatives before urgency limits your choices.
author: Joe Kelley
body:
## The date is only the start

A lease expiry creates connected decisions: stay, renew, renegotiate, relocate or change the amount and type of space. Examine those choices before an option date or delivery programme turns the decision into a rush.

There is no universal lead time. Start by checking the actual lease and the operational work required.

## Record the controlling dates

Find the commencement and expiry dates, option window, notice requirements and review dates. Record the source clause for each. If the document is unclear, ask a commercial property solicitor to interpret it.

## Understand the current obligations

Identify rent and reviews, outgoings, security, repair, assignment, option and make-good provisions that could affect the decision. This is commercial planning as well as legal review, and each adviser should stay within their role.

## Update the workplace brief

Record what the business needs now: team size, work patterns, customer access, storage, technology, accessibility, location, budget and timing. A clear brief makes staying and moving easier to compare.

## Compare credible paths

Compare the full commercial and operational picture rather than headline rent alone. Include fit out, furniture, downtime, professional advice, make-good and the obligations carried through the term. Label assumptions and confirm current figures before committing.

## Work backwards from delivery

Legal review, approvals, design, procurement, fit out, furniture, technology and the move itself can affect timing. Work backwards from the date the workplace must operate.

A useful first action is to record the expiry and option dates with their clause references, then write down the business decision you need to make.

This article is general information, not legal or financial advice.
